title: CI3 Sessions — Load, Set, Use, Destroy
description: The four basic session moves in CodeIgniter 3, and the $_SESSION global underneath them.
congratsText: You mastered the CI3 session basics!
objectives: Load the session library before touching the session
Set a value with set_userdata and read it back with userdata
Say where CI3 keeps the values ($_SESSION)
recap: Load: $this->load->library('session'); in every method that uses it.
Set: set_userdata('key', value) — setting the same key again replaces it.
Use: userdata('key') reads it back anywhere, returns NULL if unused, and is the same value as PHP's $_SESSION['key'].
Destroy: sess_destroy() empties the box, no arguments, no undo.

chunks.text: A session is a small box of values the server keeps for one browser, even after the page is gone.

check.question: Who holds the values in a session?

chunks.text: Nothing works until you load it: $this->load->library('session');

options: Set a value in the box

chunks.text: That load line goes in every method that touches the session — check(), home(), logout(). No shortcut.

chunks.text: $this->session->set_userdata('username', 'maria'); puts a value in the box. First part is the key, second is the value.
The value usually comes from the form: login() shows it with $this->load->view('login_form');, then check() reads it with $this->input->post('username');.

check.question: Which method stores the typed name?

chunks.text: Set the same key twice and the second value replaces the first. The box keeps one value per key.

chunks.text: $this->session->userdata('username') reads the value back. It returns NULL when that key holds nothing.

check.question: What comes back for an unused key?

chunks.text: It works in any method, even one the form never reached. home() has no post data at all, yet it still prints the name.

check.question: Does home() need the form to get the name?

chunks.text: CI3 keeps that box in PHP's own global array, $_SESSION. So $_SESSION['username'] holds the exact same value as userdata('username').

chunks.text: $this->session->sess_destroy(); throws the whole box away. It takes no arguments and it cannot be undone.
